title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Russian classic with soured cream
excerpt: Tender strips of sirloin in a rich, tangy sauce of soured cream, mustard, and mushrooms. Stroganoff comes together in under 30 minutes and is best served over buttered egg noodles or fluffy rice.
sourceNotes: Beef stroganoff takes its name from the Stroganov family of Russian merchants and is recorded in Russian cookbooks from the mid-nineteenth century. The dish spread internationally during the twentieth century and became a staple of mid-century dinner party menus across Europe and America.

content.text: Slice the beef as thinly as you can, ideally 3 to 4mm thick, against the grain. Thin slices cook through in seconds and stay tender; thicker pieces can become chewy. Cook the beef in a single, very hot layer so it sears rather than stews. Add the soured cream off the heat to prevent it from curdling.

items.prepNote: very thinly sliced against the grain

content.text: Pat the beef strips dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a very high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer for 1 minute per side until browned. Work in batches; do not crowd the pan. Remove and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and mushrooms, increase the heat, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the mushrooms are golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard and stir for 30 seconds.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the soured cream until the sauce is smooth and combined.
Return the beef and any resting juices to the pan. Stir gently over a low heat for 1 minute to warm through. Do not boil.
Scatter with chopped parsley and serve immediately over egg noodles or basmati rice.

items.symptom: Soured cream has curdled in the sauce.
items.cause: It was added while the pan was still very hot.
items.fix: Always remove pan from heat before stirring in soured cream.

items.cause: It was not sliced thinly enough or was overcooked.
items.fix: Slice paper-thin; sear for 1 minute each side only.

items.symptom: Mushrooms are wet and not golden.
items.cause: The pan was overcrowded or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cook mushrooms over high heat in a single layer; do not stir too often.
